clue.text: Goodly portion may be taken by a worker

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in a farm hand
some means a portion or part of something

explanation.surface: A labourer may be handed a generous share of the takings.
explanation.walkthrough: The charade is written in clue order reversed in sense: the portion is 'taken by' the worker, so the worker's word comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodly in its old sense means good-looking or considerable, just as a fine-looking person or a large sum is described.

clue.text: Anyone breaking into a computer system will be cut with little hesitation

definitions.text: Anyone breaking into a computer system

parts.note: to hack is to cut roughly
er is the short sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A computer intruder is warned they will be slashed without a moment's pause.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who gains unauthorised entry to computer networks is called by this name.

clue.text: The point of a record player

definitions.text: The point of a record player

parts.words: The point of a record player
parts.note: reads like asking what a gramophone is for, but means the sharp tip that runs in the groove

explanation.surface: A question about why anyone would own a gramophone.
explanation.definitionFit: The stylus of a gramophone, the sharp tip that tracks the groove, is also called by this sewing-tool word.

clue.text: Hospital worker and nurse go out together

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two colleagues on a ward start dating each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is the anagram signal on NURSE and GO; 'together' is a link that completes the surface of a couple going out.
explanation.definitionFit: An operating doctor is a medical staff member employed at a hospital.

clue.text: Face a doctor with superior bearing

parts.note: MO stands for medical officer, a doctor
U means upper-class, socially superior, in British usage
E, east, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: Confronting a physician who carries himself loftily.
explanation.walkthrough: U as 'superior' is the British upper-class label (U and non-U); compass points like E serve as bearings.
explanation.definitionFit: A pout is a grimace, and to pull such a pout is to make a face.

clue.text: Rested badly -— this is discouraging

indicators.note: badly signals the letters of the word are poorly arranged and must be reordered

explanation.surface: Someone slept poorly, which is disheartening.
explanation.definitionFit: To discourage someone from acting is to put them off, a synonym relation.

clue.text: Such a beast may well get chained

indicators.note: suggests the word chained may end up as something else, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dangerous animal is likely to be shackled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may well get' is the anagram signal: the letters of CHAINED rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The spiny anteater of Australia and New Guinea is an animal, a beast in the clue's sense.

clue.text: A break for everyone taking part

definitions.text: A break for everyone taking part

parts.words: A break for everyone taking part
parts.note: reads as a rest for all participants, but means the interval between acts of a play, when the cast all pause

explanation.surface: A pause in an activity so all participants can rest.
explanation.definitionFit: This French theatrical term names the interval between two acts, a rest for the performers.

clue.text: Judgement delivered in a few words

definitions.meaning: a grammatical unit made of several words

explanation.surface: A verdict summed up briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge pronounces a penalty, and a grammatical unit of words carries the same name.

clue.text: Get rid of listening equipment concealed in sock

indicators.note: one word is hidden away inside another, so one goes within the other

parts.note: to sock someone is to hit them, a clout
the ear is what we hear with

explanation.surface: A spy is told to dispose of a bug tucked inside a stocking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sock' looks like the garment but is a blow, CLOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To empty out or discard unwanted items is a phrasal synonym for disposing of them.

clue.text: Read about impact made by an old Greek's tunic

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or read carefully
a hit is an impact

explanation.surface: Reading about a collision caused by an ancient Greek garment.
explanation.walkthrough: CON as 'read' is the old sense of studying a text closely.
explanation.definitionFit: This garment was a long woollen or linen tunic worn in ancient Greece.

clue.text: Sit surrounded by refuse — there's stupidity for you!

indicators.note: means one word is placed with another round it

parts.note: to deny is to refuse

explanation.surface: Sitting in a rubbish heap is the height of foolishness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refuse' looks like rubbish but is the verb, DENY.
explanation.definitionFit: Thickness or slowness of mind is a figurative sense of this word, as in denseness.

clue.text: Gape at slim sound woman

indicators.note: sound means the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to eye is to gape at, and lean means slim

explanation.surface: Staring at a thin, healthy woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like 'healthy' describing the woman, but signals the homophone of EYE LEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a female first name, so a woman.

clue.text: Cat's tail — many animals are backed with one!

indicators.note: backed means the word is read in the backward direction

parts.note: deer are animals
M, the Roman numeral for a thousand, stands for many
an ace is a one in cards and dice

explanation.surface: A pet's tail makes a fine perch for whole herds of creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns DEER into REED; 'Cat's tail' is a plant name, not a feline's appendage.
explanation.definitionFit: This tall waterside plant, the bulrush, is also called cat's-tail for its furry brown spike.

clue.text: Implements poor accommodation in sea-going craft

indicators.note: in places the shabby dwelling inside the vessel letters

parts.note: SS, steamship, is a sea-going craft
a hovel is a wretched dwelling

explanation.surface: Equipment includes miserable cabins on ocean liners.
explanation.definitionFit: Spade-like tools for digging and moving loose material are implements.

clue.text: Keen to serve thin sauce. It's different

indicators.note: different means made into something else, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A diner is eager to offer a runny gravy, saying it is unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: Eager and passionate about something means keen.

clue.text: Carol is without money but discerning

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: to carol is to sing
a cent is a coin, money

explanation.surface: A carol singer has no cash but good judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' here, but it is the old sense 'outside', so the singing word wraps the coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Detecting by smell, sensing, is a way of perceiving or picking something out.

clue.text: Send for a drive?

definitions.meaning: to send someone is to delight or transport them
a driveway is the way in to a house

explanation.surface: Dispatching someone out for a ride in the car.
explanation.walkthrough: Stress the first syllable for the driveway sense and the second for the delight sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchant or thrill someone is to transport them, and a driveway is a way into a property.

clue.text: Traditionalist wanting jam brought round at four

indicators.note: means one word is placed around the others

parts.note: conserve is jam
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned person wants preserves served at teatime.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone resistant to change and holding to tradition is so described.

clue.text: From Castile originally, so resilient

indicators.note: originally implies the letters came from a different arrangement, so they are reordered

explanation.surface: Something hailing first from Spain is hard-wearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From ... originally' suggests origin, but signals a rearrangement of CASTILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Springy material that returns to its shape is resilient.

clue.text: Shake and strive to restrain an unruly youngster

indicators.note: to restrain is to hold in, so one word holds the other inside

parts.note: to vie is to strive or compete
a brat is a badly behaved child

explanation.surface: A parent struggles and shakes trying to control a naughty child.
explanation.definitionFit: To quiver or tremble rapidly is to shake.

clue.text: Coin at one time used as a special gift

definitions.meaning: an ancient unit of weight and money in Greece and the Near East

explanation.surface: An old coin offered as a present.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient monetary unit and a natural flair share the name, the latter from the biblical parable.

clue.text: High-minded individual interrupting a fellow just to annoy

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into the middle of another word

parts.note: Peter stands for any man's name
S stands for saint, a person of lofty virtue

explanation.surface: A prig butts in on a man merely to irritate him.
explanation.walkthrough: S for saint is a standard abbreviation, as in St Peter.
explanation.definitionFit: To bother or irritate persistently is to annoy.

clue.text: Associate following a pattern usually

indicators.note: following means the associate word comes after the pattern word

parts.note: a norm is a standard pattern
an ally is an associate

explanation.surface: Usually one keeps to the pattern of one's colleagues.
explanation.definitionFit: As a rule, ordinarily, means usually.

clue.text: Dedicated person arranging outside broadcast at the last minute

parts.note: late means delayed, at the last moment

explanation.surface: A conscientious producer organises a live remote broadcast at the eleventh hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranging' is only a link here and signals no rearrangement; the two pieces simply stand side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A layperson devoted to a religious community, dedicated to monastic life, bears this name.

clue.text: Not working for nothing

explanation.surface: An idle person working without pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle and at liberty is one sense; costing nothing, gratis, is the other.

clue.text: Writing hotel a note is quite natural

parts.note: an inn is a hotel
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Writing a note to a hotel comes naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writing' is only part of the surface picture and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Inborn and instinctive, present from birth, means natural.

clue.text: Get rates negotiated. Most important!

indicators.note: negotiated suggests the terms are worked over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A business buyer urges a deal on price as the top priority.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of great means of the most importance.

clue.text: In general people agree certain changes are needed in this country

indicators.note: In signals the answer is tucked within the following words

explanation.surface: Most people accept that the nation needs reforms.
explanation.walkthrough: The country sits inside 'agree certain'; the rest is surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mediterranean nation, so a country.

clue.text: He keeps on saying a salesman should go along with the consumer

parts.note: rep is short for sales representative
an eater consumes food

explanation.surface: A man repeats that the salesman should agree with the customer.
explanation.definitionFit: One who says the same thing again and again does this habitually.
